- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3) and price is trending upward, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — adjust downward 2–5% for first 3 days of positive sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window — apply 2–5% downward bias to first 5 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to ignore underlying bearish momentum — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.
